Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


How does Voter Cap get played on an unsuccessful referendum?

Anyway, Voter Cap seems to be an obstacle to making any balanced PA cards with
costs. The few I've attempted have been backed into the corner of textual
acrobatics like Eldest Command Undeath. Even that is suspect due to the option
of alternating referendums between the costly-ones and the Voter Capped ones.

Voter Cap itself may be the problem.

It is the only card that grants such easy blood gain (repeatable, unblockable,
restrictions amounting only to: if your deck is working in its primary goal in
the first place). And then it compounds the effect with pool gain to boot.

Other comparable effects:
Taste of Vitae: successful combat damage. No pool.
Giant's Blood: MPA, once per game, no pool gain.
Fifth Tradition: P/J, action, 1 blood cost, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
Entrenching: action, 4 blood already, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
Concert Tour: DoC (not many big-cap DoC), action, 1 blood, delay, no pool.

The closest seems to be Taste of Vitae, which is a pretty powerful card, I think
we all agree. It also gives blood for nothing more than "what you were doing
anyhow". It is slightly more cyclable (can be played even when damage is
prevented or not done at all or whatever), but it never gives pool, and it's
harder to get the same range of gain with damage compared to vote margins, and
vote margins don't incur the same risks as combat (and, arguably, "doing what
your deck does" is typically stronger in the "oust your prey" category for vote
decks than for combat decks).

Thoughts?

Messages.Author: Darby Keeney
Messages.Body:
On Feb 3, 8:38 am, LSJ <vtes...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
> Anyway, Voter Cap seems to be an obstacle to making any balanced PA cards with
> costs.

Basically true, if the cost is blood or pool. Less true if the cost
were neither. Here are some examples of alternate costs to consider:

- Only usable as your first non-manatory action of this
turn" (usability restriction)
- Your turns ends immediately at the (successful) conclusion of this
referendum (no discard phase, and maybe no more actions depending on
timing)
- Only usable as your first non-manatory action of this turn.
EFFECT. Your turns (or minion phase) ends immediately at the
(successful) conclusion of this referendum" (restriction, loss of
actions and discard)
- Only usable by a vampire of capacity greater than 3. EFFECT. This
vampire is burned if this referendum is successful"

Alternately, I don't recall pursuing the analog of bleed modifiers for
voting yet.

- No (further) action modifiers may be played during this action.

Just some food for thought.

> Voter Cap itself may be the problem.

>From the tenor of your following comments, I infer that you may
believe Voter Cap is problematic. I wish to offer a different
perspective.

Yes, Voter Cap is quite good. In fact, I would suggest that VC is
often more worthwhile then the vote itself.

Why? Because most vote effects are relatively weak for the effort
involved. That's why all we typically see at the upper level of play
are KRC, PTO and once-per-game votes - they MAY be worth the overhead
of getting them to work (especially in multi-act or Majesty decks).
That seems to be the thrust of the initial post - getting rid of one-
dimensional voting, though I understand how you can be concerned about
creating "very good" votes with the presence of Voter Cap (pun
intended) in the game. Perhaps if those new (powerful) votes employed
the restrictions offered above, a balance might be reached without
"jumping through hoops" - a la Eldest Command Undeath.

Personally, I believe that Voter Cap's strength is well-balanced by
how difficult it usually is to optimally use. Consider:

- You must be playing PRE (OK, that's not a stretch in real voting
decks)
- You must have a vote, or a table vote, to call (KRC, PTO or a once-
per-game vote in tournaments)
- You must not be blocked by 2 people (usually requires some type of
action modifier)
- You must pass the vote (either with lots of big titles minions,
significant overhead in making titles, in-hand action modifiers or
excellent interpersonal skill + intelligent other players)
- You then hope to have the Voter Cap in hand
- You hope that none of this stuff can be Delayed, Eyed or DI'ed

Yes, you can get by with some missing pieces. But if those missing
bits cause even one link in the chain to fail, handjam will quickly
lead to your demise. If you're multi-acting (a good reason to want
blood recursion), you now have another dimension of complexity to
layer in.

I suppose you can call Rumors of Gehenna, name all the voters and
potential blockers and hope they're silly enough to all vote for it
allowing you to VC. Good tables pass your vote by 1 when they see the
voter has [PRE]. If you want big numbers with VS, you must dependably
generate large vote numbers yourself.

To that end, I believe that Awe is more problematic than Voter Cap,
given their synergy.

> Other comparable effects:
> Taste of Vitae: successful combat damage. No pool.

Taste of Vitae enables most of its deck archtypes to work. With the
exception of ranged combat decks, you can't count on a lot of big-
bolus pool gain (Minion Tap) from it. With the exception of Awe-
driven decks, Voter Cap doesn't stricty enable its deck archetype.
They both seem really great, but with greatly different intents to me.

- many ToV = my minions can keep fighting, as my deck requires.
- many VC = I can gain enough pool to not carry a sizable body of
Wakes and bleed bounce, thereby allowing me to fit votes + stealth +
vote mods + Voter Cap in my deck.

> Fifth Tradition: P/J, action, 1 blood cost, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
> Entrenching: action, 4 blood already, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
> Concert Tour: DoC (not many big-cap DoC), action, 1 blood, delay, no pool.

These don't even come close - they require an action - not simply
happening as a by-product of your deck's primary focus.

> Thoughts?

Pretty clear.....
- I would like to see more tournament worthy votes, even if they offer
signiciant non-blood, non-pool costs
- Voter Cap is fine - any deck that carries several must become more
focused on voting to use it well, thereby sacrificing something else.

I look forward to a spirited debate.

Darby

Messages.Author: Daneel
Messages.Body:
On Sat, 03 Feb 2007 15:38:05 GMT, LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote:

> Anyway, Voter Cap seems to be an obstacle to making any balanced PA
> cards with costs. The few I've attempted have been backed into the
> corner of textual acrobatics like Eldest Command Undeath. Even that is
> suspect due to the option of alternating referendums between the
> costly-ones and the Voter Capped ones.
>
> Voter Cap itself may be the problem.

While I'm not a big fan of Political decks, and I do agree they
can indeed be overwhealming if given room to build up, I'm not
sure I agree with the conclusion.

> It is the only card that grants such easy blood gain (repeatable,
> unblockable, restrictions amounting only to: if your deck is working in
> its primary goal in the first place). And then it compounds the effect
> with pool gain to boot.
>
> Other comparable effects:
> Taste of Vitae: successful combat damage. No pool.
> Giant's Blood: MPA, once per game, no pool gain.
> Fifth Tradition: P/J, action, 1 blood cost, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
> Entrenching: action, 4 blood already, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
> Concert Tour: DoC (not many big-cap DoC), action, 1 blood, delay, no
> pool.

I'd probably also mention Renewed Vigor, as that is also fairly repeatable,
and is mainly restricted by the scarce bloodline discipline required to
pull it off.

> The closest seems to be Taste of Vitae, which is a pretty powerful card,
> I think we all agree. It also gives blood for nothing more than "what
> you were doing anyhow". It is slightly more cyclable (can be played even
> when damage is prevented or not done at all or whatever), but it never
> gives pool, and it's harder to get the same range of gain with damage
> compared to vote margins, and vote margins don't incur the same risks as
> combat (and, arguably, "doing what your deck does" is typically stronger
> in the "oust your prey" category for vote decks than for combat decks).
>
> Thoughts?

I think voting is supposed to be harder than combat. Combat: you do a (D)
action, and then whack the opposing minion with almost no possibility of
interference from the other players (barring mostly D.I., which is IMHO
a rather problematic card I wouldn't like to build any argument on). If
you chose the right target - and chances are, at least one of the players
whose whacking is beneficial to your game are susceptible - you can gain
blood pretty easily. With politics, you have 4 potential adversaries,
who - if playing smartly - will make sure your Voter Captivation doesn't
net you much more than a Life in the City would.

Sure, Voter Cap does make it pretty hard to build a cost onto Political
cards, which might be a real pain from a designer point of view, so I
guess that angle does merit some consideration. But outside of this I'm
unconvinced that Voter is the issue, and not, for example, Minion Tap,
Anthelios, ease of getting powerful vampires with a gazillion votes, or
any other aspect of the game.

Anyway, that's my 20 cents. From a player point of view I'm far more
concerned by the continuous strengthening of passive play (e.g. walls)
than by any other phenomenon. A Wall has access to bloat options similar
in power level to Tap+Cap, except it needs more cards for the setup, but
then needs no cards to operate. It also arguably bloats simply by doing
its game. But I digress...

--
Regards,

Daneel

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <x%1xh.6667$zH1....@newssvr29.news.prodigy.net>, LSJ

<vte...@white-wolf.com> writes:
>Anyway, Voter Cap seems to be an obstacle to making any balanced PA
>cards with costs. The few I've attempted have been backed into the
>corner of textual acrobatics like Eldest Command Undeath.

It may be helpful to separate two different things here:

1) High Stakes cards, with punishments
2) Straight-forward higher costs.

(Obviously, the two can mingle - a higher cost card that has a
punishment.)

There are two ways of approaching this, that can potentially apply to
both situations.

1) Textual acrobatics. This is not inherently a bad thing, and could
potentially be simplified to something like "The acting minion cannot
play action modifiers on this referendum" or "Action modifiers cost the
acting minion two additional blood" or something - not perfect, but
would cause problems for a Voter Cap heavy deck. Or more targetedly
"Action modifiers requiring Presence cannot be played on this action."

2) Non-pool costs. Note that I am not suggesting the following examples
are super-balanced, but I'm just trying out mechanics. (In some ways,
these are verbal acrobatics, but they're way less direct.) For example:

Hostage Negotiation
Political Action, 1 stealth, 1 vote
Requires a ready vampire with a Bomb.
Choose a ready Methuselah. If this referendum is successful,
that Methuselah takes 3 pool damage. If they control a ready
mortal, they take 4 pool damage instead. If not, this vampire
takes 5 damage and goes to torpor. Burn the bomb at the end of
this action, regardless of how it ends.

So the VC can mitigate some of it (get blood back), but you need a bomb,
you need a get out of torpor if it fails, and so on.

Character Assassination
Political action, 1 stealth, 1 vote
Requires a ready titled vampire
Choose a ready minion. If this referendum is successful, put
this card on the chosen with X Character counters, where X is
the number of votes this acting vampire's title is worth (or 1
if they are a Priscus). If the referendum is not successful,
put this card on the acting vampire with twice as many counters.
If the vampire with this card bleeds for more than 2, the bleed
is capped at 2 (ignore the excess). If the vampire with this
card casts more than 1 vote, they are capped at 1 vote. Remove
a Character counter during your untap phase, and burn the card
when it has zero counters.

VC doesn't really help here at all.

Census
Political action, 1 stealth, 1 vote
Unique
If this action is successful, do not conduct a referendum. Put
this card in play and choose two clans. During your next minion
phase, if you control this acting vampire and he is ready, he
must take an action to call a referendum. If that action is
successful, conduct a referendum; the terms of the referendum
are that you gain pool equal to the number of ready minions in
the game for the two chosen clans. (This second referendum
cannot be called in any other way; this card remains in play
and does not burn, but contributes one vote to this second
referendum.)

Two actions, unique, can get rid of the vampire in between time (as was
attempted with RtoI, for example), blah blah.

Bringing Down The House
Political Action, 1 stealth, 1 vote
You must choose a ready location you control when announcing
this action. If that location was a piece of equipment, it must
be on this acting vampire. Choose a ready Methuselah. If this
referendum passes, each of that Methuselah's ready minions takes
1 damage. If this referendum passes by more than 5 votes, each
of that Methuselah's ready minions takes 2 damage instead. If
any minions leave the ready region because of this, gain a pool.
Burn the location you chose at the end of this action.

VC will let you pay for one, but extra master phases or equip actions,
or whatever.

Defend Thy Own Kinsmen By Smiting Others (Please Turn Over)
Political Action, 1 stealth, 1 vote
Requires a ready Kholo, or a vampire with a title worth at least
3 votes.
Choose a ready vampire with a capacity less than 5 or an ally
with a cost less than 4. If this referendum is successful, burn
the chosen minion and, after the action has finished, burn all
the blood on this vampire. If the referendum is not successful,
remove the acting vampire from the game.

Anti-VC verbal acrobatics (the vampire empties are VC would be played),
and a severe punishment clause.

The All-Night Session
Political Action, 1 stealth, 1 vote
Some devestating referendum ability.
Before the referendum is conducted, put this card on the acting
vampire. The vampire with this card does not untap. If an
effect would untap this vampire, the untap part of the effect is
ignored. Burn this card at the start of your next minion phase.

No Freak Drive, can't trivially act next turn - Rutor's Hand or
Precognizant Mobility or whatever. Or even Metro Underground! Anything
that makes Metro Underground a borderline consideration can't be all
bad...

(Standard disclaimers: All my own work, White Wolf are welcome to use,
etc.)

> Even that is suspect due to the option of alternating referendums
>between the costly-ones and the Voter Capped ones.

With an indirect cost, I don't think that would be significantly
problematic. Yes, VC would mean you could pay more for Bombs or
locations, but you still need them in hand to equip, and so on.

>Voter Cap itself may be the problem.
>
>It is the only card that grants such easy blood gain (repeatable,
>unblockable, restrictions amounting only to: if your deck is working in
>its primary goal in the first place). And then it compounds the effect
>with pool gain to boot.

It's unique in that regard, but uniqueness alone would not be a reason
to act alone.

>Other comparable effects:
>Taste of Vitae: successful combat damage. No pool.
>Giant's Blood: MPA, once per game, no pool gain.
>Fifth Tradition: P/J, action, 1 blood cost, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
>Entrenching: action, 4 blood already, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
>Concert Tour: DoC (not many big-cap DoC), action, 1 blood, delay, no pool.

Festivo dello Estinto: potentially huge amounts of blood, once per game,
multiple actions, available to other Methuselahs.

You also have to factor in that Fifth, Entrenching and Concert Tour do
not require a successful referendum (which can be interrupted with e.g.
Delaying Tactics).

>The closest seems to be Taste of Vitae, which is a pretty powerful
>card, I think we all agree. It also gives blood for nothing more than
>"what you were doing anyhow". It is slightly more cyclable (can be
>played even when damage is prevented or not done at all or whatever),
>but it never gives pool, and it's harder to get the same range of gain
>with damage compared to vote margins, and vote margins don't incur the
>same risks as combat (and, arguably, "doing what your deck does" is
>typically stronger in the "oust your prey" category for vote decks than
>for combat decks).

Sort of. But Taste is also disciplineless where - perhaps? - the
comparison is supposed to be Bribes.

Also, Taste is usable in almost every combat deck, whereas Voter
Captivation is only usable in PRE decks - which is a lot of vote decks,
but the bigger problem is the synergy Presence has with vote push. Awe
was designed after Voter Captivation by people who didn't know what they
were doing, which makes one of the most powerful vote push packages in
the game. Aside from Theft decks and Ally combat, pretty much every
combat deck in the game can (and very possibly should) use Taste -
whereas there are a wide range of non-Presence vote decks, which do
okay.

One option might be a possible Event that fiddled with politics, or some
other hoser that was disproportionately heavy on Presence.

>Thoughts?

I'm not sure I'd like to see Voter Captivation undermined by a rewrite.
It's very good, but I don't think it's too good. That is, I'd probably
write it differently if I were writing it now - perhaps put it in play
with those counters, and get everything at the start of your untap phase
(so that a combat deck has an easier time hitting a mostly empty vampire
etc., and if the VC were *on* the vampire, it could stop everything with
a burn...).

But I'm not sure it's a place where errata would be appropriate. I'd
rather see alternative costs, and potential extra cards for non-Presence
vote strategies so that Presence isn't *quite* so far ahead of
everything else.

--
James Coupe

Messages.Author: CthuluKitty
Messages.Body:
> Anyway, Voter Cap seems to be an obstacle to making any balanced PA cards with
> costs. The few I've attempted have been backed into the corner of textual
> acrobatics like Eldest Command Undeath. Even that is suspect due to the option
> of alternating referendums between the costly-ones and the Voter Capped ones.
>
> Voter Cap itself may be the problem.

This strikes me as a fairly reasonable conclusion given the overall
power level of the blood/pool gain in combination with the successful
use of votes. The claim that political actions are generally lower in
power level than their difficulty justifies, and that Voter
Captivation is necessary to balance this, is absurd in my view. While
bleeding may have a higher payoff per action, it too is susceptible to
risks including aggressive bounce and Archon Investigation. Votes
also allow flexibility due to cards like Disputed Territory,
Banishment, Consanguineous Boon, and others. Combat is well behind
both, much to my continual chagrin.

I'd also like to suggest that a possible result of in some way nerfing
Voter Cap would be a reduction in game-crippling table talk in fairly
common tournament situations. The whole process of trying to let
votes pass by the minimum amount, and the mental arithmetic involved
in figuring out how much a vote is passing by (as opposed to simply is
it passing or not) can stall the game, and I'd expect fewer time outs
if Voter Cap were either less frequently played or somehow altered.

One possible proposal to fix both problems would be to assign a fixed
number to the blood/pool gain on Voter Cap. Such a solution would
reduce the time spent handling referdenda, and would curtail the most
abusive uses of Tap n Cap without completely nerfing the card, or PRE
vote in general.

For example:
Voter Captivation
action modifier, pre
Only usable when a referndum called by the acting vampire is passing.
pre: The acting vampire gains 2 blood.
PRE: The acting vampires 3 blood, up to 2 of which you may move to
your pool.

Comments?

Messages.Author: d
Messages.Body:
I'd like to just see clan specific vote cards. Start with Nosferatu,
something like:

Tales from the Crypt
+1 stealth political action
Requires: Nosferatu
Allocate 3 points among any number of methusalehs. If successful, the
chosen Methuselahs may (or must?) draw the allocated number of crypt
cards (no cost is paid).

Gangrel Consensus
Requires: Gangrel (duh!)
+1 stealth political action
Choose a sect. If this referendum is successful, all Gangrel in play
must change to that sect or burn 1 blood. Put this card in play. Any
Gangrel entering play may choose to change their sect to the chosen
sect. If the chosen sect was independent, any untapped ready
independent Gangrel may burn 1 blood to become Anarch when this
referendum passes. Votes by non-gangrel minions and effects which do
not require Gangrel each count for 1 less vote in this referendum.

Changing the Wheels
Requires: Malkavian
+1 stealth political action
If this referendum is successful, put this card in play. When another
methusaleh calls a referendum with terms, you may burn this card to
set the terms of the referendum and gain 3 votes in that referendum.
Only one Changing the Wheels can be used this way in a game.

[I like this restriction over 'one played per game' because it is
slightly more useable and cycleable if you then choose to put 2 of
them in your deck ]

Apportioning an Old One
Requires: Tremere antitribu
+1 stealth political action
If this referendum is successful, the acting vampire gains two blood
and every Methuselah may search his or her library for a Master:
Discipline card and place it on a vampire the same age or younger
than the acting vampire.

I'd like to hear other ideas for these clans and more. Staying
topical, start with the clans who don't have PRE as a common
discipline. Important voty Lasombra have pre, and so do some
Assamites and Tscimisce, so think about that when coming up with card
costings if any are needed in addition to the clan requirement.

I think the Ventrue and (!)Tor should get boring votes like:
If successful, put this card in play, you may tap it when it is ( is
not) your turn to gain 1 vote.

And as far as Voter Cap, I would hate to see it altered, as I consider
it one of the fundamental cards of the game (although I hardly ever
build decks with it, honestly). If it wasn't around, I'd build even
fewer political decks.

And a word on some of the suggestions that have come up in this
thread, I certainly like some of the ideas in the suggested cards.
I would just put this out there to consider though: especially
powerful effects should be balanced with costs and opportunity
restrictions, but wildly powerful cards with very high costs/play
restrictions arent especially fun. (Not fun to be so difficult to
play, and not fun to be completely hosed by one play even if it was
difficult to pull off). Going too far in that direction just makes the
game erratic and unpredictable rather than Strategic. For instance,
the initial card suggested - allocate 5 points KRC style - is probably

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija

In article <1170534950.1...@h3g2000cwc.googlegroups.com>,
as...@hotmail.com wrote:

> I do not think the strenght of Voter Cap should prevent you from
> making fun, balanced political action-cards. Is it really so now?

In a design sense, making Political Actions cost blood or pool is mostly
irrelevant, because of Voter Cap--the most effective vote decks are
already using Presence (for Bewitching, Awe, and, ya know, Voter Cap),
so if a vote is made to cost a blood or two blood or a pool or whatever,
that cost is virtually a non issue--you call the vote, you push the vote
through however is necessary, and then Voter Cap to get the blood and/or
pool you spent back. The result is that presumably, when designing a
political action card, if they want it to have a cost in blood or pool,
they either need to:

A) Make the cost absurdly high (like, say, a minimum of 3 pool, so that
the Voter Cap doesn't just make it a wash, in which case the card is
likely to be completely unplayable in non Presence based vote decks).

B) Use ad-hoc "you can't use Voter Cap" on this vote wording, like on
Eldest Command Undeath.

Voter Cap also makes cards like Awe much more powerful than likely
necessary--Awe is already powerful, in that it can allow you to push
through pretty much any vote you want against pretty much any reasonable
opposition. The cost of this is supposed to be that it costs a lot of
blood. But 'cause every blood you spend gets you 2 votes (at PRE), you
can spend all your blood for a ton of votes, and Voter Cap it all back
and then some. Yeah, once and a while, someone will DI the voter cap, or
Delaying Tactics the cote after all the blood is spent, but most of the
time, Voter Cap just makes Awe a total no brainer.

Voter Cap is akin to these theoretical cards:

Bleeder Cap
Action Mod
Only usable when a bleed is successful.
[dom] The acting vampire gains blood equal to the amount of Pool lost
from the bleed.

pool.

Combat

possibilities.

balancing the cost of combat cards.

> Personally, I believe that Voter Cap's strength is well-balanced by
> how difficult it usually is to optimally use.

Agreed. Voter Cap is yet another moving part in a deck type that
already has a lot of factors that can go wrong for it. It's strong,
but not overwhelmingly so relative to its opportunity cost.

> - I would like to see more tournament worthy votes, even if they offer
> signiciant non-blood, non-pool costs
> - Voter Cap is fine - any deck that carries several must become more
> focused on voting to use it well, thereby sacrificing something else.
>

Agreed. I do think the vote aspect of V:tes is one of the more
stagnant parts of the game. Vote decks and technology, and the vote
meta-game hasn't changed much since Ancient Hearts. Most vote decks we
see today could have been built 10 years ago. This is a area that
could use a shake-up and some designer love.

Part of the problem is the Jyhad votes (KRC, Con Agg, Con Boon, Parity
Shift) are so strong that anything stronger would be broken. And
anything weaker is DOA.

(Old combat cards -- .44 Magnum, Torn Signpost, Carrion Crows have
similar dominance in the combat space).

Fuctional vote decks are so space intensive that casual vote and
toolbox vote don't really work. The votes must be the main offensive
weapon. Votes that don't lead to the ousting of your prey don't tend
to be worth the effort.

Options for changing the vote game dynamic:

Weaken older cards (KRC - divide 3 point points... )
Create more non-Presence voter-cap like effects, and sucesssful vote
rewards
Create cards that invite use because they are flexible or overcome
typical Vote-deck problems (Votes with +2 stealth, or worth 2-3 votes)
Or action mods that provide stealth and/or votes (or allow muliple
Political Cards with a single action?).

-Ben Swainbank

Keep in mind that Taste *has* been nerfed in recent history (only one

strike, Taste, gain some blood, strike again, Taste a third time if you

after a greedy Awe or something, but most of the time, if your deck is
going (i.e. you get to call and pass votes, even if once and a while,
you get blocked or voted down), the opportunity cost of Voter Cap is
pretty insignificant.

anything. Maybe limit the blood/pool gain (like was done with 5th
Tradition) to a fixed number (maybe at inferior, gain 2 blood and at
superior, gain 2 blood and 2 pool or something). Or limit the number
that can be played per turn (only 1 Voter Cap per turn or something).

> Wasn't that more a clarity change (get rid of the post-strike "Taste"

Very possibly, as the Jyhad version of Taste is wildly confusing (i.e.
based on the wording, what happens if you play 3 at the same time, which
lead to a lot of rulings on the card, which eventually ended up with the
new wording).

> The
> power change was relatively minor - especially compared to the
> proposed Voter Cap changes.

It was less minor than you probably think--the change in *when* Taste
happened had a huge impact on non Celerity combat (in the old days, the
Nosferatu could fight the Brujah toe to toe with excessive use of Taste,
as you could Taste *before* additional strikes). Now you need to survive
the whole round to play Taste. Which is no small nerfing.

> If you assume the opportunity cost has already been met, then yes, its
> pretty insignificant at that point.

I mean, like, you are correct in that *voting* as a strategy has a
pretty high opportunity cost (i.e. if you get blocked or can't pass your
votes, your deck is mostly dead cards). But assuming you can play your
deck (i.e. you can generally get through unblocked and generally pass
votes, even though either of these might not happen occasionally), Voter
Cap is little more than another greasy wheel.

> My Voter Cap inner monologue tends to something like: There's a Voter
> Cap. Good. I need the pool and blood. Now I need to find a vote. Ok.
> Got a vote card. Hmm.. going to need some stealth to get this off.
> Crap. My prey just brought up another Prince. How can I talk this vote
> through to get my Voter Cap off...

Sure. But that is the same for pretty much *all* cogs in a vote deck.
"Hey! I have this cool vote card. Now I need a stealth card to get it
past that blocker. And then a Bewitching to make it pass." Or "Hey! I
have a Bewitching, an Awe and a Voter Cap! If only I had a vote to
call..." One of the costs of vote decks in general is that they tend to
have a lot of moving parts that need to all be in the right place at the
right time. Voter Cap is just another part that needs to be factored in.

> I play a lot more combat decks and always play with Taste of Vitae,
> which is much easier to cycle, and tends to provide a very useful
> effect (even if you don't "win" the combat round).

Sure. Taste is really good. But as LSJ pointed out earlier, Taste has a
pretty significant opportunity cost ( which I would claim is more
restrictive than Voter Cap due to the inherent risks of combat i.e. you
need to get into a fight and survive till the end of the round and do
damage to your opponent) that balances it out. And it doesn't nullify
the cost of combat cards in the same way that Voter Cap nullifies the
cost of, say, Awe--I generally don't play, like, Pushing the Limit in
combat decks specifically 'cause the 1 blood cost makes it that much
more likely that you'll get torped and not get to play Taste. I don't
have such reservations about Awe.

> I think political actions could have other requirements/costs instead
> of a blood cost to make them balanced.

Sure, but giving them a blood/pool cost is the most obvious (and
logical) way to balance out a card, and the existence of Voter Cap
pretty much completely removes this tool from the arsenal of the card
designers in regards to Political Actions.

> For example:
>
> Pool cost

Unless the Pool cost is high enough to counteract the pool gain from the
Voter Cap, it is, like a blood cost, mostly irrelevant. And giving a
card a pool cost that balances out the card with Voter Cap is likely to
make the card wildly unplayable by non Presence vote decks. For example,
how good would a PA card have to be to justify a 3 pool cost? And how
good would it have to be to justify using it in a non Presence vote deck
at a 3 pool cost? Likely pretty good. Which would probably make it
either too good to put in a Presence vote deck, or not good enough to
put into a non Presence vote deck.

> Tapping another vampire you control
> Keeping the acting vampire from playing further action modifiers
> during this action

Both of these are reasonable, but likely require a lot more testing and
balancing than simply enabling the designers to add a blood/pool cost to
a PA card that they currently can't realistically do.

> If you want to create a political action playable by non Presence vote

It isn't just that it is the easiest solution. Voter Cap is, in and of
itself, arguably too powerful. As noted earlier, compare it to Taste and
5th Tradition (both of which have been significantly altered since their
original introduction, unlike Voter Cap which is still the same),
Giant's Blood (which has a significant limitation from day 1), Concert
Tour and Entrenching (which have both been designed recently, and have
significant limits built into them). Voter Cap is a wildly powerful card
that somehow has managed to avoid the tweaks that hit most similar cards
of the same era.

> Exactly, it requires a lot more testing and balancing than simply
> changing Voter Captivation because of lack of imagination.

Lack of imagination isn't really the issue here (see Eldest Command
Undeath--not an elegant solution, and not one that I would like to see a
lot of. But certainly imaginative)--if a standard paradigm of card
design (i.e. making a card cost blood/pool for increased effect) is cut
off due to a single, arguably overpowered card, and fixing that card
will both make it less overpowered *and* restore that tool to the
designers, the solution seems obvious. At least to me.

It's probably worth noting that the more significant problem with VC, as
reflected in "why isn't it worthwhile to make vote cards cost
something", is its ability to refill the calling vampire, as opposed to
the "gain 2 pool" aspect. Given the ease of pool recursion in this game
(Blood Doll, Minion Tap), it's important to consider that ANY card which
grants blood to a vampire is only one step away from actually granting
pool to that vampire's controlling Methuselah.

Given the above...

LSJ wrote:
> Only usable after resolving a successful referendum.
> [pre] The acting vampire gains X blood from the blood bank, where X is
> the number of votes by which the referendum passed, up to a maximum of 2.
> [PRE] As above, but up to a maximum of 4.

This still reads "Gain 4 pool".

> Only usable when referendum passes by at least 2 (after resolving the
> referendum).
> [pre] Gain 2 blood.
> [PRE] Gain 2 pool.

As another poster noted, this doesn't speed up the "do math during the
referendum to prevent Voter Cap" step any, and possibly increases the
number of stumbling blocks to actually running a vote deck unnecessarily.

> Only usable after resolving a successful referendum.
> [pre] Gain 2 blood.
> [PRE] Gain 2 pool.
>
> The last one opens up VC to auto-pass votes as well, which it currently
> fizzles on.

In general, I like this, though the auto-pass quirk will certainly make
it interesting. However, it might lead to more use of auto-pass vote
tech overall (something often avoided because of the inability to play
Voter Cap, interestingly), and possibly even lead to the idea of things
like Praxis Seizure seeing play again in a midcap voter deck as the TAIL
end of an autopass vote, instead of as an innocuous run-up.

If nothing else, it should speed up the "do math" stage of the
referendums; either you like the outcome or you don't, and it also will
remove the "why won't you vote in favor so I can Voter Cap for more"
whining stage, something I was heartily sick of well over four years ago.

- --
Derek

On Feb 3, 7:38 am, LSJ <vtes...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
> Voter Cap itself may be the problem.
>

> It is the only card that grants such easy blood gain (repeatable, unblockable,
> restrictions amounting only to: if your deck is working in its primary goal in
> the first place). And then it compounds the effect with pool gain to boot.

Yes. It seems incredibly good for all vote decks with PRE as
currently written.

> Other comparable effects:
> Taste of Vitae: successful combat damage. No pool.
> Giant's Blood: MPA, once per game, no pool gain.
> Fifth Tradition: P/J, action, 1 blood cost, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
> Entrenching: action, 4 blood already, only 4 blood gained, no pool.
> Concert Tour: DoC (not many big-cap DoC), action, 1 blood, delay, no pool.

Maybe these were already mentioned, but also consider Renewed Vigor,
Restoration, and Regeneration.

> Thoughts?

Ooh, LSJ asking for design input - I love it! This game is so great,
and LSJ is awesome. It's really incredible that the CCG designer is
asking for open input from players.

My thoughts:
- I agree that Voter Cap is overpowered.
- I like the idea of simplifying the card to work whenever the vote
passes, regardless by how much (or at least 2.)

A specific card idea that requires minimal change is:
- Play before any votes are cast. If the referendum is successful...

That way, if the vote fails or is delayed, you've wasted it. I think
that makes for a bit more interesting interactions between DT and vote
cancellations, too.

To weaken it even more, it could be played when the vote action is
announced, and then people would know to block it.

If I were designing, I would make it most similar to Restoration, and
would choose:

Play during a referendum before any votes are cast.
[pre] If this referendum passes, gain two blood.
[PRE] If this referendum passes, gain three blood.

I think the pool gain aspect is the biggest issue, so that's what I
would remove.

If that seems too weak, then perhaps:
Play during a referendum before any votes are cast.
[pre] If the vote passes, the acting vampire gains X blood from the

blood bank, where X is the number of votes by which the referendum
passed, up to a maximum of 2.
[PRE] As above, but up to a maximum of 4.

If pool gain seems appealing, then I would pick:
Play during a referendum before votes are cast.
[pre] If the vote passes, the acting vampire gains 2 blood.
[PRE] as above, and gain 1 pool.

Making this change also encourages non-presence based vote decks; as
things stand now, I have to have very strong reasons not to include
PRE and voter cap in a vote deck.

For any of the above texts, I would still play with the card (I
think), but not as many.

Ira

I have to pull off manually, I have better things to include in a deck.

> I think the pool gain aspect is the biggest issue, so that's what I

See other post. The blood gain is the biggest problem.

For example, if you suddenly made, say, PTO cost 4 blood to call, and
turned Voter Cap into a 1-pool/2-pool card, is there now a significant
cost to calling and passing PTO? Obviously, there is; especially if you
need to use a card like Awe.

Contrast with existing VC, where you refill the vampire _and_ possibly
still gain 1/2 pool.

> If that seems too weak, then perhaps:
> Play during a referendum before any votes are cast.

I wouldn't play this card.

> If pool gain seems appealing, then I would pick:
> Play during a referendum before votes are cast.

I wouldn't play this card. You may have noticed a theme here; when you
force people to throw out a big ol' "This vote should not be allowed to
pass" before votes are cast, then you force them to create table
hostility. Sure, right now everyone still reflexively assumes that
someone is going to Voter Cap, but the card's sheer strength makes it
worthwile to do it anyway and just include enough push to make sure it
always passes, table hostility be damned.

If you weaken the card, however, you make it less likely that 8 have
been automatically included in the deck -- and as such you provide an
opportunity for people to just Play The Game, instead of feeling like
they have to anti-vote just to cut down on the Voter Cap. Forcing the
card to be played before votes are cast removes the uncertainty.

- --
Derek

"LSJ" <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:nxLxh.

> Where "less drastic" becomes blurred with "inconsequential".

Scott, you seem fixated on how overpowered Voter Cap is. I empathize
with your concerns in finding consistent ways to create cost/value
relationships, but I'm still hazy about how overpowered the card is.

Question: Is Voter Captivation really that dominant in a competitive
environment?

Analysis: I did a quick word search on Lasombra's TWDA, with the
following results for occurrences of the following phrases:

Blood Doll 503
Minion Tap 230
Govern the Unaligned 188
Majesty 160
Kine Resources Contested 134
Taste of Vitae 120
Freak Drive 118
Voter Captivation 86
Kindred Spirits 45
Perfectionist 36

Voter Captivation and most of the associated tournament-worthy votes
have been around since Dark Sovereigns. Yet only 65% of the decks
that employ KRC employ Voter Captivation. Voter Cap is much less
"abused" in winning decks than Govern the Unaligned. Taste of Vitae
shows up more often. Given this trend, I fail to see how Voter
Captivation creates a dominant game-winning deck archetype.

So the perception of "overpoweredness" most come from something other
than the competitive environment.

I'll extrapolate - and I believe it comes from two issues:
- the creation of a powerful pool gain loop (with some pool reward
for actually passing the vote)
- a preconception that the cost/benefit of a card must be derived
from blood spent by the acting vampire. Therefore Voter Cap, which
negates that cost (and to lesser extents Ancara Citadel and
Perfectionist) are overpowered.

I understand that 5th Tradition was nerfed for that first reason
alone. But 5th Traditon/Forgotten Labyrinth was much easier to pull
off than Vote/Forgotten Labyrinth/Awe (table-talk)/Voter Cap - so I
expect a greater reward from Voter Cap than 5th Tradition. Yes, I
maintain this despite claims that Voter Cap is a "freebie" because you
can play it when your deck does what it is supposed to - pass votes.
It's not a freebie. When one uses Cap extensively, one sees the high
opportunity cost this card represents - when things go wrong, you're
stuck with a crapload of in-vote cards and nothing else. Then, you
die. High (hidden) cost, high reward profile. Sounds OK to me.

As for that second point, yeah that's tricky and a pain in the hind
end from a designer's viewpoint. Hence I can understand your
conviction that Voter Cap is a problem actor. But there have been a
plethora of other cost options discussed that might serve to alleviate
your angst. I encourage you to explore some of them.

My fear remains that your proposals will turn a staple card that
encourages voting into something that most of us would never put in a
competitive deck. Even worse, until new high-quality votes are
offered, it will completely neuter the already-difficult-to-design-and-
play vote decks, rendering them unworthy of tournament play. And yes,
I maintain that votes decks that do something other than Praxis/KRC/
Cap at 1 stealth (e.g., the good decks) are difficult to build and
play.

So, as you consider possible "fixes" - remember that your nerfbat is
much heavier than you might think. 5th Trad certainly knows this -
it's cornercase/wallpaper these days.

Looking forward to even more interesting dialog,
Darby

> ...

We should consider the possibility that Voter Cap avoided the tweaks
because it isn't TOO powerful. Powerful, true, but not overpowered or
undercosted, certainly not enough to justify a change based on (what I
believe to be) only the design team's issues in designing new votes, a
valid issue, regardless.

oldTaste of Vitae required only combat, and it could be played at multiple
times during the round -- a 1-card "combo". old5th Tradition required
only a Prince/Justicar and (probably) some stealth -- only a 2-card combo.
These were cards with powerful effects that were arguably overpowered
and/or undercosted.

Voter Captivation requires a vampire with pre/PRE, then:
1. a vote card
2. (probably) some level of stealth
3. an Awe or Bewitching Oration
4. success in the referendum
5. the Voter Cap

So, a conditional 4-card combo, and G-d forbid that you're trying to vote
with non-stealthy presence voters. To compare it to old5th and any
version of Taste is to not understand the level of difficulty of pulling
off the Voter Cap, not to mention the fact that voting decks, like
dedicated-Combat decks, are incredibly card-intensive, and very careful
consideration should be taken to determine whether or not changing one of
their important cards, lest you make those decks significantly less
playable.

Have dedicated-Combat decks been so weak that Alastor, Dogs of War,
Perpetual Care, Dragonbound, Carver's Meat Packing, Frontal Assault,
Haqim's Law: Judgement, Yawp Court, Red List and Trophies, and all the new
'Action: (D) may enter combat' cards needed to be created to enhance their
effectiveness, and dedicated-Vote decks are so strong that Voter
Captivation all by itself needs to be changed? I don't see it.

On Feb 5, 11:53 am, "Ben Swainbank" <bswainb...@hotmail.com> wrote:
>

>
> Weaken older cards (KRC - divide 3 point points... )

> typical Vote-deck problems (Votes with +2 stealth, or worth 2-3 votes)
> Or action mods that provide stealth and/or votes (or allow muliple
> Political Cards with a single action?).
>

I don't think this post should be dismissed out of hand when the other
option is nerfing a long-standing, often-played card. And
specifically a card that, in many ways, makes voting worth doing at
all. Not saying that VC definitely should stay the way it is, but
what about some other options?

Maybe new cards that will make Voter Cap less useful (a bit of a
tangent to Ben's post)... sure, this is like the "DI Defense" that
says that nothing is broken because you can always DI it. You would
actually have to play with the VC hosers in order for VC to actually
be any less powerful, and the hoser cards would have to be useful in
other ways, too. A few ideas:

Strangulation
Reaction
Requires a ready Anarch vampire
tha: The acting vampire may not gain blood during this action. Any
blood he or she gains goes to the blood bank instead.
qui: The acting vampire may not gain blood during this action. Any
blood he or she gains goes to the blood bank instead.
pot: The acting vampire takes 1 damage. If this causes the acting
vampire to go to torpor, the action fails. No cost is paid.

Anarch Threat
Event
Non-anarch vampires may not gain blood except by hunting, or from
Hunting Ground cards. Any blood they gain goes to the blood bank
instead. During each methuselah's untap phase, that methuselah may
move one blood from any of his or her vampires to this card. Burn
this card when there are 5 blood counters on it.

Heated Debate (preferably a picture of a vampire with blood dripping
from its fangs and hands)
Reaction. Frenzy, played on this reacting vampire.
Requires a ready vampire. Only usable during a political action
before votes are cast. If the referendum passes, the acting vampire
takes X damage, where X is the number of votes by which the referendum
passed.

And regardless of whether or not VC is nerfed, or whether some other
course of action is taken, I definitely do like the idea of some votes
with additional benefits. Something like a 3-point KRC that is called
with +2 stealth or that gives you +2 votes. Free States Rant is also
a good example of a vote card that changed the voting scene to a
certain degree - very nice vote that is called by an Independent
vampire (who is likely to be untitled), and reduces the value of
titles and increases the value of the Edge. I certainly wouldn't mind
seeing more creative votes along the lines of FSR.

On Feb 6, 8:33 am, "Damnans" <damnansv...@ono.com> wrote:
> Too powerful for what?

Too powerful compared to other cards that refil your vampires. Most
other cards the refil your vampires are:

-Limited in effect (only give you a small amount, like 1-4)
-Highly conditional (only work in a small number of situations)
-Limited in use (only once per game)
-Take an action (that action does nothing but give you blood)

Voter Cap isn't like this. You gain a lot of blood (combined with Awe,
you refil completely) *and* some pool. All while taking an action that
is probably injuring your prey anyway (KRC?). It doesn't require an
action that doesn't hurt your prey. It can happen multiple times per
turn. It works if your deck is working at all. Its effect is only
limited by the number of Awes you own. It is a highly unrestricted,
unlimited, hardly conditional card that happens while your deck is
doing what it wants to be doing anyway.

> Both, but those combos are not automatic. There are some requirements
> involved (e.g., you don't get 2 pool every time you play a vote).
> Sometimes your votes get blocked, or don't pass, etc.

Sure. But as mentioned before, if your deck is doing what it is meant
to be doing (i.e. calling votes and passing votes), the additional
cost to play Voter Cap is insignificant (i.e. have one in your hand.
Yeah, sometimes you get blocked. And sometimes you get voted down. But
that is an issue with vote decks as a whole, and isn't actually a
problem for Voter Cap. If your deck is going, you can play Voter Cap.

> The fact that bringing out a high capacity vampire is a big pool
> investement, means that you need effective ways to get that pool back,
> if you want to bring out more vampires and take more actions per turn.

So you Minion Tap and get blood back in ways that other non Presence
enabled big vampire decks do (Giant's Blood; Entrench/Freak;
whatever). Other decks use big vampires. That don't use Voter Cap. And
they survive.

> Such as?

Nosferatu Royalty--there are multiples of these in the TWDA (mind you,
my version that is in the TWDA has Presence in it :-). Sabbat
Cardinal. Non presence backed All IC decks. They exist. And are
playable. And don't have Voter Cap. And I don't think there is any
discussion here of eliminating Voter Cap, just reducing its effect.

And if it is hard to pull off Voter Cap for a reasonable amount as you
seem to think it is, isn't making it just give you 2 blood or 2 pool
on any successful vote (like the best candidate for the change) an
*improvement*?

-Peter

Messages.Author: Malone
Messages.Body:
(1) I don't find the wording of ECU even slightly byzantine, on the
contrary it is simple and straightforward. I don't think it even
suffers from the appearance of having to work around a single other
card (although, apparently, that was the situation) because it also
prevents blood gain from Guru or Perfectionist, for example. If a
card's design wants a blood cost that can't easily be offset, what's
wrong with adding a few words that say so? That a vampire can still
get back the cost by alternating ECU one turn, KRC with Voter Cap next
turn is not a bad thing. If you can call and pass a referrendum by 8
votes every turn, and have VC on hand when you need it, you deserve to
be full of blood!

(2) Comparison to action cards or master cards that say "gain X" or
"fill to capacity" is not germaine, as VC is an action modifier that
requires things to have happened other than (but including) not being
blocked.
Taste, on the other hand seems an apt analogy. Yes, combat is
much riskier than a referrendum, but blood gain is more immediately
helpful to a fighter than to a voter. And Taste can 'pay' for combat
cards that cost blood almost as well as VC 'pays' for votey cards that
cost blood. (Sure, Taste is less likely to generate windfall profits
because inflicting 10 damage doesn't generally return 10 blood. But
excepting Awe, which I believe is the actual problem, it's easier to
inflict 10 damage than to pass a referrendum by 10 votes.) The
biggest difference seems to be that Taste is disciplineless. If the
restriction of VC to Presence is a problem, neutering VC is not really
a solution.

(3) Voter Cap + Minion Tap: This has been with the game since day 1,
and I like it.

(4) Voter Cap + Awe: This is obviously broken, and easy to fix. Add
a "no further action modifiers" clause to Awe.
The longer a card has been around, and the more common it is in
the hands of beginners and casual players, the worse the trouble
caused by functional changes to its wording.

(5) The awkwardness and delay of wrangling over how much a vote will
pass by when it's clear enough that it will pass is the only strong
argument for changing VC, and not a sufficient one in my opinion.

Messages.Author: d
Messages.Body:
I just want to weigh in STRONGLY AGAINST changing Voter Captivation.
Political decks are not the strongest decks out there, Voter Capping
political decks are not necessarily the strongest political decks.

Also, as mentioned earlier in the thread, coming up with votes that
could cause more pool damage than current votes is the wrong
direction. ConAg is a very powerful card, balanced by the fact that it
becomes almost worthless in the end game. Parity Shift is a very
powerful card, balanced by its title and pool requirement (to oust
with Parity Shift you have to first put yourself in danger of being
ousted - although Parity Shift + 2x KRC in a turn is a recipe for
ousting in 1 turn so is 4x KRC with no title or pool requirement).

Voting doesn't need more instant pool damage effects. Instead, voting
needs new avenues to enhance other game mechanics and dealmaking, to
replace the banned Kindred Restructure and so on.

Also, and this is only a marginal side argument: of LSJ's three
proposed options, the 3rd is simplest:
pre: Gain two blood.
PRE: Gain two pool.

I think its not a justified card change. But also the direction it
goes in seems to be away from more balanced voting and towards
supporting weenie votes (because using Voter Cap rewards using high
capacity vampires - a _good_ design feature).
Since weenie voting is an arguably problematic deck archetype, I don't
think the world's various metagames would benefit from a card change
that encouraged the move towards weenie voting instead of large tap
and cap decks.

I mean, really, people don't complain about Tap and Cap decks being
broken. They make nice targets for combat decks, and they can be
summarily ousted by big early bleeds and remain vulnerable to stealth
or swarm bleed.

So, to wrap up.

1) Please don't change our venerable old Voter Captivations.
2) Please don't add even bigger pool damage cards or easier to use
ones.
3) Please do add new interesting voter dynamics and political actions.
Again I suggest clan specific political actions as one avenue to
explore. I think the discussion on "interesting" restrictions has also
been useful.

I wouldn't mind having a small set of new political action cards that
banned Presence (and Melpominee?) action modifiers. Some with capacity
restrictions wouldn't go amiss either, especially if all of them
didn't *directly* affect pool.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
On Feb 6, 10:19 am, LSJ <vtes...@white-wolf.com> wrote:

>
> The idea is that the "fix" to Voter Cap would be chosen so as to not weaken
> decks that should be viable "too much".
>

This is important, I think. The thing is, voting decks can be very
strong, but they are certainly not "obviously overpowered" at this
point. Most good voting decks make use of Voter Cap (that is, those
that are capable of winning fairly reliably), to some degree or
other. So if Voter Cap is reduced in power, it seems likely that
voting in general will need to gain some other advantages at the same
time, otherwise politcal actions may well be absent from the
tournament scene for years. Some of the ideas for "more versatile
votes" could certainly help there.

And if voting strategies are given a boost to make up for the loss of
Voter Cap, then we may well see some more varied voting decks being
played - such as the ones without Presence, since they couldn't use
Voter Cap before anyway. Something like Assamites with Alamut, maybe
more Lasombra voters that don't graft on presence (not that they were
extremely weak before), Akunanse bruise & vote, etc... Maybe
Daughters voting will finally be viable (I've tried so hard, but it
just tends to suck for one reason or other)... even though they have
Presence for VC, their low capacity limits its usefulness, and their
lack of inherent votes can be hard to overcome. It all depends on
what kind of boost is given to voting, and to what degree.

To me, none of that is necessarily a bad thing, but I think that the
solution to Voter Cap is more complex than simply saying, "okay, X is
2... we don't have to worry about that anymore."

Incidentally, the Misdirection equation was solved with X = 1, the
Voter Captivation equation may soon be solved with X = 2. I wonder
what other constants the V:TES universe holds. Perhaps the Eldritch
Glimmer constant? Planck's addendum to Minion Tap? Newton's Law of
Lightning Reflex Motion? Just curious... ;)

Messages.Author: The Name Forgotten
Messages.Body:
What I find interesting about voter cap, is that if there were a vote
that would do the same thing, I would definitely stack a whole batch
of them in most vote decks anyway - even if the vote still had the
[pre/PRE] requirements.

I.e. If there was a card like:

Vote Captivation
Political Action

[pre] The acting vampire gains X blood from the blood bank, where X is

the number of votes by which the referendum passes.
[PRE] As above, but move up to 2 of those blood counters to your pool
instead of this vampire.

I'd still think it was a fairly powerful card.

The fact that Voter Cap is attached to a mechanic that a [pre] vote
deck is going to have regardless, is, as LSJ points out, incredibly
powerful. At the moment, nothing I've seen bloats as well, or as
consistently, as a good [pre] vote deck. Voting does have the downside
of having to contend with the rest of the table, but there are just so
many types of decks around, and especially with v few/no votes, that
many vote decks have almost no trouble passing there votes anyway.
More often the threat is having everyone gang up on them and beat them
into submission.

That being said, the biggest reason why I think voter cap is
considered powerful is thanks to two other cards which it is often
used in combination with. The first is Minion Tap - which leads to
major bloatage, and the second is Awe - which helps you pass your
votes in huge margins.

In fact, if I were to suggest a change to make Voter Cap less
powerful, it would actually be to nerf (I hope George Lucas doesn't
sue us all for this term) Minion Taps - maybe make it so that you can
only pull a max of 3/4 blood, or restrict it to smaller cap vampires
(less than 8 cap), or tap the vampire to move blood, or even a clause
that says the vampire cannot gain blood for the rest of the meth's
turn (blood gained goes to blood bank instead). It would help slow the
ridiculous bloatage of voter cap decks. I don't often see many other
decks that use minion taps that really capitalise on Minion Taps as
much as Voter Cap decks, and for most of them, pulling 3/4 blood off,
or waiting a turn, would be fine anyway.

We all know the ridiculousness comes in when you can consistently
minion tap Arika for 10, call a vote, bewitching, and voter cap all
the way to her capacity again. And when there's a horde of 3rd
Traditions and you are calling consag boons, you could gain more than
half of your starting pool amount easily in 1 turn with only 1 minion
voting. I'd like to find any reason why someone would consider such a
feat, that is so readily accessible to any [pre] vote deck, to not be
powerful.

Aren't there enough ways for vote decks to bloat anyway? I mean,
there's consag boons, anarch salon, anathema (which is also a v
powerful bloat mechanism), ancient influence, Autarkis Persecution,
Diversity, Finding the Path, Parity Shift, Political Flux
(potentially), Political Stanglehold, Reins of Power, Tithings,
Transfer of Power & Honor the Elders. I grant that many of these don't
show up in decks (and are here for the sake of completeness), but
others are in most vote decks I know, especially big cap ones.

I also play a v powerful [obf] Ventrue deck, so I am v familiar with
the ridiculousness of the card. No other deck I have ever built (well,
since the fifth tradition change-over days) has ever had close to the
amount of bloatage I get off of that deck - which is why it is one of
the few decks that I keep built (without changing/tweaking), and it's
almost certainly the longest standing deck I've got (about twice as
long as any other deck I've got built). For some people who have tons
of cards and decks aplenty, this might not mean much, but I am very
fickle with my decks, and I change them constantly, that is, with the
exception of that one.

In short: I wouldn't like to see the card changed, but I do think a
change would be justified.

Pool costs not so much - because there's a hard cap on the amount of

because it's not terribly hard in a PRE deck to make a vote pass by

this isn't what I'd normally call a "hard" cap, there's an upper bound
to the amount you can gain back no matter how many damage increasers
you play on your strike. VC has no such thing - every additional vote
is always an additional blood.

against the referendum, or half the capacity of the acting vampire, or
the amount of pool/blood burned as a result of the referendum, it
would be far more comparable to Taste.

Tactics/DI, and I'm pretty sure we don't need anything *better* than
Delaying Tactics to stop it.

more votes to cut back on Voter Captivations with (and then expect
people to play with these cards specifically to cut down on Voter
Captivations so that political cards with blood costs actually
matter), doesn't that suggest that VC should be changed instead?

Voter Captivation is a scaled effect with a greater effect benefited
by vampires of greater capacity. The game suffers signifigantly from
an imbalance in power towards many minions being more viable than a
few minions. More minions means more actions, and more actions means
more ousting power, and more ousting power results in quicker games.

One of the fundamental problems that the original designers saw in the
game was that the game took too long to play and was too complicated.
Quicker games are a result of more minions acting. Things that slow
games down are intercept, combat and bloating.

So to make games quicker intercept must be toned down, combat must be
streamlined and bloating must be eliminated.

Perhaps that wasn't what you were asking for?

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <R8Pxh.16054$zH1....@newssvr29.news.prodigy.net>, LSJ
<vte...@white-wolf.com> writes:
>James Coupe wrote:
>> I don't think the Design Team + Playtesters feel they can't try out
>> interesting requirements and balance them, and I'm not sure why they
>> couldn't do the same with political actions, if they chose to.
>
>There is no "choose" for political actions, since Voter Cap removes the
>choice. So-called "interesting" requirements are the only option, so
>not really a matter of "choice" at all.

No, that's not true. If, as you've suggested elsewhere in the thread,
political actions and politics in general have become stagnant *and*
that that stagnancy is dependent on VC, and the only way to resolve that
is to give cards a cost and therefore nerf VC to allow that to be
meaningful, then I'd tend to disagree.

The *other* choice is there to create other cards that do radically
different things. For whatever reason, the amount of originality in
political actions in the WW era has been low, in my opinion. Note that
this is specifically political actions. There has been a veritable
mountain of creativity in other areas - Events, Nights of Reckoning,
non-unique vampires, the Bloodlines and the mountain of amazingly cool
stuff there, Anarch three-ways, dual-discipline cards, Trifles - but
political actions have just been left alone. And I don't think it's
just because of cost.

I've just done a very swift search for political actions in the WW era.
As I see it:

Alastor - the cheap equipment is good, but it's a sort of Archon/Templar
Anarch Salon - pool and blood gain
Auto-da-Fé - mini-PTO or poll loss
Blood Seige - "stealing" a title, which is kind of cool but quite
sketchy due to needing a Prince out
Brinksmanship - brand new, and quite interesting, with a 1 pool cost
Crusades - several new ones. More of the same, but the "untap in your
discard phase" thing is quite cute, instead of increased
capacity
Deploy the Hand - damage to a minion, which is similar to Free States
Rant (though different in execution)
Diversity - a variant on Con Boon
Dogs of War - new and cool, but it's another enter combat vote
Eldest Command Undeath - PTO
Finding the Path - sort of interesting, though it's mostly just pool
gain fiddling, and quite weak
Firebrand - actually very cool. It has the vote bolstering angle, but
it also has the cool new untap angle.
Free States Rant - good and interesting when it was introduced
Hand Intervention - potentially cool, though a bit restricted. New for
politics.
Hierophant - Camarilla Exemplary and a vote booster
Honor the Elders - pool and blood gain
Overseer - a twist on Praxis Seizures, but in essence just a vote gainer
Perpetual Care - new and interesting! And no pool cost or blood cost,
but has two interesting costs - needing to get those minions
into torpor, and needing to find yourself without other
Methuselahs about to be ousted by indiscriminate damage. A
good, solid, interesting card. Yes, it's a pool burner, but
it's very interesting in how it goes about it.
Rabble Razing - interesting, but a sketchy include. It would be nice if
it had been slightly more flexible so that you could include it
and still use it if the weenies don't turn up. (Sat between the
Imbued and a fatty deck, say.)
Reinforcements - good and cool!
Reins of Power - reverse Ancient Influence
Secret Must Be Kept - sort of a twist on Kindred Segregation, though
could be really quite good with it (no repay clause)
Seraph - interesting, but only as good as the cards it enables and,
prior to SoC at least, Seraph has been a little lack-luster
Snipe Hunt - see Rabble Razing
Sweeper - interesting, but seeing the top card of a deck is usually not
considered that powerful
Trumped-Up Charges - similar to Seraph, it's only as good as the trait
it bestows
Watchtower - pool gain, though it's an interesting variant on it for
political decks
Year of Fortune - hand size increase, which is interesting, though not
highly valued by players

So what does that amount to?

- We have a bunch of the bread-and-butter cards, pool gain, blood gain,
vote gain
- We have some damage votes, but none of them are hugely exciting
- We have a couple of recent attempts at cards similar to PTO
- More ways to enter combat
- Variants on existing cards (Camarilla Exemplary, Kindred Segregation)

What's actually new?

- ash-heap diving (new to politics)
- minion damage votes (Free States Rant is very good, Deploy the Hand is
somewhat lacklustre because it doesn't give you the control - if
it was something like "If you control a ready Seraph, you
choose", a la Baltimore Purge, it might have been much cooler)
- untap tech (Firebrand)
- plus and minus hand size
- Perpetual Care is a real boon to rush/vote decks, and not just another
way of allowing them in the first place

And, erm, well. These are new, but they're not *that* cool. One of
Garfield's design considerations for political actions was that they
should be a bit of a curve ball. Blood loss, pool loss, blood gain,
pool gain... it's not that curvey.

Ash-heap diving *is* curvey. Untap tech is also curvey. Though these
aren't wildly offensive, they are cool. Perpetual Care is potentially
curvey. Plus and minus hand-size is curvey without being super
powerful, and so doesn't see all though much play.

But then go back and look at non-WW sets. We'll exclude Kindred
Restructure and Dramatic Upheaval, though they were interesting, radical
options for vote that weren't available elsewhere. While they are, in
the fullness of time, a bad thing, the key facet of them being unique is
not a bad thing.

Banishment - very curvey, hot, interesting minion control tech. Could
we disable other things?
Disputed Territory - location theft. Perhaps other things could be
stolen by political actions?
First Tradition - out of left field, interfering with a Methuselah's
ability to take a turn!
Masquerade Enforcement - stopping influencing out vampires
Lextalionis - Punishing players for winning
Peace Treaty/Kindred Segregation - shutdown other resources
Rumors of Gehenna - improve your own master card strategy
Political Flux - dick with the benefits of ousting players
Reversal of Fortunes - fun, silly card that empowers a couple of really
screwball strategies
Anathema - sort of borderline. Thing is, it empowers a vote/rush
strategy, making it a solid deck type to explore, rather than
just facilitating it (a la Archon, Templar, Alastor, Dogs of
War), so is sort of routine (pool gain) but sort of new
Sabbat Inquisitor - sort of cool, a weird ability and +bleed, in one
package

Compared to this sort of weird-ass stuff - some of which is dross,
obviously - the WW political action cards look quite stifled. And that
would be an entirely different way of approaching this issue. Don't
look at costs, look at what you're achieving with Political Actions -
and, more specifically, look at what you're not even attempting.
There's very little there that's really innovative or unusual.

Crazy example: Heart of Nizchetus is a super popular card. Everyone
loves it! But it's equipment. What if it had been printed like so:

Freedom of the City
Requires a vampire with a city-based title
Political Action, 1 vote, 1 stealth
Unique
If this referendum is successful, put this card on the acting
vampire. If the vampire with this card is ready during your
untap phase...

Fun and innovative for a vote deck to try out? I'd have thought so.
Pretty balanced? Well, it can't be stolen, but it requires a city title
and a successful referendum, so it's probably about right, maybe a small
tweak or something, but I don't see it as hideously unbalanced.

Honestly, the sorts of things that vote actions have done in the WW era
have been quite timid in doing radical, unusual things. You don't need
to go into costs to try to un-stagnate votes.

Going into costs is one choice you can make. But it's not the only
choice.

>But if:
>1) Voter Cap is overly powerful
>and
>2) The existence of overly-powerful VC unnecessarily limits design
>
>then the obvious course of action is to fix VC.

1) hasn't been proved. That Voter Cap is very useful is certainly true.
That it was overly broad in its design is certainly arguable. But I
don't think you've made a solid case that it's overly powerful. Just
that for its deck type (Presence-oriented politics), it's a very popular
include. But then, there are a lot of similarly broad cards which turn
up in an awful lot of decks. Dominate bleed finds it hard to stay away
from Govern the Unaligned, and it's hard to design good new bleed cards
that aren't Govern the Unaligned. It's hard to design meaningful bounce
that isn't Deflection - people will still just graft Dominate onto their
decks. That it's very good for its archetype isn't the same as it being
overly powerful.

Since there are still design avenues to explore, I'd rather we explored
them *before* nerfing VC.

- If leaving VC as it is for the time being forces some unusual,
difficult costs to be explored, I don't see that as a limit I
care about right now, really.

- If being unhappy with unusual costs means that radically different
avenues are explored at zero cost, I'm happy with that too.

--
James Coupe

I never said VC is broken. Please re-read my post.

IMO VC is just one step below being overtly broken. VC is the one card
that enables to bring out your complete crypt of 10-11 caps (Arika,
Queen Anne, Leandro, etc.) *without* going to great lengths to
generate pool. With VC you can play your deck - call KRCs, Parity
Shifts, PTOs, ConAgs and so on - and as an *added benefit* you get
pool/blood (with Minion Tap you convert blood to pool easily, and I
have never seen decks that heavily use VC that do not use MT as well)
to boot.

Other decks have to take actions to get that blood back on their
vamps: Restoration, 5th Tradition, Concert Tour and others. Which do
not further their primary goal of ousting their prey, mind you. And
those actions can just as easily blocked like political actions.
So I don't see why the delivery method is stressed when talking about
political actions, and overlooked in context with "other" actions. PAs
have normally +1 stealth to begin with...

If you want to stop VC consistently, you have to play with DI or DT,
assuming the deck using VC is built with getting VPs in mind and is
working at least moderately the way it is expected to.

Arika playing Ancient Influence generates 6 pool. That alone is huge.
Naturally good PRE vote-decks are using Awe and BO in abundance to
make sure their votes pass. Putting VC into this mix generates another
2 pool (that makes 8 pool during a single action!) and fills Arika up
to 11 blood (part of that will again be used for Minion Tap, say 7
blood). Now, this single action resulted in increasing your pool by
15.
Lets say you use KRC instead of Ancient Influence (to do direct damage
to your prey) you'd still get 9 pool (always assuming the MT in the
next turn, mind you). As an *added benefit* to doing furthering your
primary goal - ousting your prey.
No other card has that potential.
In my book, that makes it a no brainer, a must have, and too powerful
an effect.

The game can have powerful cards, it is not a problem in itself. And
even if it were I think that Blood Doll, Governs, Signposts and a lot of
other stables are even more powerful than Voter Captivation.

Voter Captivation enables big cap voters to bloat. They need this
ability since their focus on voting will thin their combat, interception
and/or bounce options. If not in terms of disciplines then in terms of
deckspace.

In order to avoid all political decks to devolve into breeder decks and
using con boons - a concept that is already viable - I hope you can find
a better solution than changing VC to whatever real or perceived limits
VC inflict on new vote card design.

I see a lot of people saying that presence vote is supreme compared to
vote not using presence as if it is a bad thing. I for one think it is
okay that Toreadors and Ventrues outvote Nosferatus - after all a
ventrue is less likely to draw out your beast and rip your head off.
Even if the two cammy voter clans are subject to widespread scorn I
think it will ultimately be a loss for the game if these clans could not
vote as efficiently as they can now. That means with an unchanged voter
captivation.

In order to expand on the costs I have a few suggestions that could
replace the (real or imagined) futility of pool/blood costs.

- clan requirements
- no action modifiers can be played during or after referendum
- does not untap in the next minion phase
- need to give up the edge (like reverend vote)
- reduce capacity of acting vampire with X
- change the default stealth of the action
- each ready minion controlled by the acting vampires controller take damage
- acting vampire is removed from game after succesful referendum
- burn an uncontrolled vampire / loose 4 transfers during next influence

and so on. it must be possible.

What i would not like is to have some nice cool vote card only be usable
by some obscure bloodline with no good reason other than voter captivation.

Theme votes are fine - like Dogs of War - but any general utility votes
á la banishment, KRC, Disputed Territory and so on need to be available
to the camarilla, including the ventrue and toreador.

Its just my opinion, of course, but i think the backstory supports these
clans having a larger control over kindred and human resources than most
of the other clans - sure there are exceptions, like the setites,
giovanni and lasombra but GENERAL votes needs to be GENERALLY available imo.

If VC restricts the design of such cards please consider my suggestions
for alternative costs. We would all like cool new cards but some of us
would also like to keep the old cool cards.

Frede

James Coupe wrote:
> In a VC/Awe combo, why is it not Awe that is overpowered?

Awe's cost/effect is actually somewhat balanced. You spend a lot of
blood off a vampire, you get a lot of votes... once.

So, avoiding the word "overpowered" since it's subjective and irrelevant
to the discussion: which card is the strongest in the Awe/VC combo? The
card that costs lots of blood for lots of votes, or the card that
removes the cost of the first one, lets you end up with more blood than
you started with, and gains you 2 pool as well?

Put another way:

How often do you see Awe played without VC in the deck?
How often do you see VC played without Awe in the deck?

> I can totally agree that VC/Awe is near the top of the power curve these
> days. But if it's decided that it's over the top of the power curve, I
> don't see that it's obvious that it's VC that's the problem. If the
> reasoning is going:
>
> - VC/Awe is overpowered
> - it would be convenient to nerf VC for reasons of design creativity so
> we'll nerf that one, even if nerfing Awe would be a better idea

I don't think that's the reasoning at all. I think the reasoning is
much more like:

- -- blood/pool recursion is too prevalent and contributes to game length
- -- VC allows blood/pool recursion for free while still moving forward at
full speed (KRC, etc.)
- -- VC renders any blood-based costing mechanism for PAs worthless
- -- so, is it possible to nerf VC without hurting big vampires and vote
decks unnecessarily?

I realize that the masses on the newsgroup aren't capable of complex
reasoning in this fashion, which is why the "overpowered" strawman has
begun littering the playing field.

- --
Derek
